title: The Last Reading of Tallow

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The slate reads one in twelve and the house keeps its count in loaves. The box goes up the road locked and the bell goes four, four and a gap; what is read aloud is not what is paid.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of Low Kiln, spoken at the last market of Tallow

where: Low Kiln and the Cross, Sill
pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-seventy-three-to-one-hundred-and-seventy-nine-day-old body carried everywhere, told by nobody; the surgeon's register colours the noticing (the firing as a theatre he cannot enter with heat kept and counted behind a screen and a gate of two bites, the carrying arm as a record in muscle that keeps weight and not cost, the file turned out as instruments laid on a towel, the figure read held apart from the figure paid, the near-saying stopped at the word as a clamp left too long) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line — the old life stays offstage — and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector or back-room interior, no Marra in Sill, no tenth stopping, no seventh hearing, no calling of the loan and no ending; the foundling stays offstage, the green is never Fenna in narration, and no name, figure or payer is given to any withholding

scenes.title: The Last Tend Opens
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital of the chapter: Day 173, Tallow 24, Fourthday, before first grey through mid-morning under the Vail kiln-house roof, at the hearth, the kiln mouth, the drying racks and the yard well. No recap of the close of Chapter 41. The boy is one hundred and seventy-three days old and five months and twenty-three days and nobody under any roof says so (T071/T072). The first smell is hot clay under tallow and wet wool; the first sound is the kiln's breath in fours with a gap, not a bell. Under the floor the carried fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy-three days (T088). Through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb — three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). Sella gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, says the house where another woman would say I, keeps the half-pace, leaves the widow's mark where it hung because a morning and a shelf are not openings, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, tells the fire it was the thaw, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, and sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, her hand resting a half-beat longer at the setting (T058/T079). The crust lies stiff and leathery two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool is frozen and unwiped; his hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water and comes down against the fold. The yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried); the trough stands bare and dark and the water is called weather; the shallow pan's gone place keeps its round ring on a tray of its own. Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while going on wanting the late because it puts off the paying, sweeps over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector without once turning along it, and no collector comes; six are counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh is held at the lip of the sill where it cannot, the small knife at the very edge with Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there is and giving it back, his chest tight since the dark (T036/T076). Nine stoppings stay nine objects and not a rule with no payer named to any, the tenth withheld, the Seed 16 breath unspent at the top of each reach and the loan uncalled (T061/T082). The three held changes — the Day 161 fraction at the damper, the Day 166 held beat beneath the loaf shelf and the Day 171 flagstone half-check — stand on three separate places and are not repeated, paired or joined (T062, T100, T036/T076). The danger gathers in the dust ground small as meal on the wrong wind, the sweetish lead edge off High Kiln and a pot giving its thin note before its time; the boy files the sound as a danger and not as a fourth near-full answer, and reads the firing as a theatre he cannot enter, heat kept and counted behind a screen and a gate of two bites with a payer whose name is not spoken. The old life stays offstage: no tagged memory and no Chicago break (T004).

scenes.title: The Dust Off the Back Room
scenes.synopsis: Second entry, second dated heading: Day 174, Tallow 25, Fifthday, before first grey into the morning at the Vail wheel-shed, the cold damper, the flagstones and the drying racks. Three or four men go low into the finger's-width-open back room before first grey and get no name; Sella carries past at the half-pace, turns no head, gives the house no name for them and does not say the room is cold. The two tellings of a counting room shut in the war stand side by side with no third telling (T065/T095). Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip; he keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, and the broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack entered by nobody (T035/T031). He speaks to the wheel before anyone (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady), tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note three turns before it leaves the wheel and withholds the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master come up on the wrong wind, who says a pot singing before its time generally sings itself out early; the knowing goes to the near-full tray, beside the hearings and never among them, advanced and not paid, and no pot is lost in the yard (T061/T082). When Sella's voice goes low and unfinished, Jorra's bent finger goes to the cold iron of the damper and waits for the sentence, then moves the tongue a hair's breadth and leaves it standing; the keeping of the fraction is remembered in the holding and not in a word, nobody speaks of the waiting and no payer is named (T062). Tarn's stroke goes on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check, and neither man names the other's silence; the three held changes stay three (T036/T076). Through the finger's-width door the river keeps its fifth low note, never counted among the hearings and never invented to stand up as a seventh; the damper is read once more as one piece of iron with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no word in Grathic that would carry both mercies in one mouthful, filed as an object joined to no kiln. At the well a woman asks what the kilns will want now the last tend is in and is given the weather, the pot and the river, never a figure (T077). The carried fire misses its fifth under the floor with its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy-four days (T088), and the boy is one hundred and seventy-four days old and nobody says so (T071/T072).

scenes.title: The Cost Sent to the Pot
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 175, Tallow 26, Sixthday, midday into the going of the light at the yard well, the drying racks, the loaf shelf and under the Vail roof. A neighbour with a wet pot asks what a firing costs set down in the Vail house; Sella glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze, does not touch it, and sends the woman to the pot with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, and the question is carried away level so nothing slops, nothing is priced and nothing is refused (T077). Another neighbour calls the morning a cold and a second says there is a wet one under it, and the argument ends where such arguments end, in weather. At the racks the yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Standing with her back to the basket and moving her lips along her own loaf row, Sella gives nobody a figure; the two unnamed gaps (the old space at the row's end and the palm's breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6), the one stiff brown-edged crust in the fold and its empty place, the shallow pan's gone place on its own tray and the field's empty place stay in rooms and on trays that do not touch, with no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause and no finger of his drawing the line (T060/T086, T097). From the basket's low angle the underside of the loaf shelf becomes a roof and the charcoal marks wait under the front edge; Sella does not reach beneath the board this day, so the Day 166 held beat stays where it was left, and the boy does not read, count or copy the marks, which wait for a hand that is not his and a day that has not come (T100 carried, not paid). At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke before her and river wind behind, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough and the rack space without explaining the turns to the basket; she sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, counts under her breath toward no opening, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, and does not look toward the bed. The widow's mark hangs where it hung and is not touched, because a dusk is not an opening and the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour (T058/T079). The fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy-five days (T088), and the boy's count stands at one hundred and seventy-five, exact, complete and unspent, spoken by nobody (T071/T072).

scenes.title: Six Counted, the Next I Don't Count
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry, fourth dated heading: Day 176, Tallow 27, Seventhday, morning through the afternoon at the Clay Yard, the yard well, the kindling under the Vail roof and the flagstones. The kilns stand at their heat in the firing month's last tend; the danger gathers in the dust ground small as meal, the sweetish lead edge on a wrong wind and the kiln's breath in fours with a gap, and no room is changed and no pot lost. Tarn takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction and tells the kindling Six counted. The next I don't count, with the small knife back at the very edge of its sill, six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh held at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence kept beside it (T036/T076). His chest has been tight since the dark; Ash is worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifts it; the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holds what light there is and gives it back; and the warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died lies cold in the clay pot in the loft, two years gone and unreconciled with the debt by not trying, which is not forgiving (T006 held). He says Yes, house to the ones who want the thaw early and the ones who want it late, agrees so entirely that no argument can find a foot, and goes on wanting the late because a late thaw puts off the paying, though the paying has stood in the ruts since the water went; his broom goes over the collector's road without once turning along it and no collector comes. The sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes to his teeth and no further: he draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, does not say the word that would call the loan, and does not stand a tenth stopping up to join the nine, because the seventh year has not yet been earned (T036/T076, T061/T082). The Seed 16 breath stands unspent at the top of each reach with its small interval where a breath should have gone in and had not. At the well a woman asks what the last firing will want and is given the weather, the river and the pot, never a figure, and the yard goes around its two unswept lines and the missing hand's place with a look and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Sella tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, and does not touch the widow's mark, because a morning and a shelf are not openings (T058/T079). The surgeon's register reads the held breath as a clamp left too long on a vessel that will not bear the taking off and the near-saying stopped at the word as a chart closed over its finding with the neat margin showing: the reading is exact and worth nothing at two paces. The carried fire under the broken pot answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy-six days (T088), and the boy is one hundred and seventy-six days old and nobody says so (T071/T072). The old life stays offstage, no tagged memory and no Chicago break (T004).

scenes.title: An Inventory That Is Not a Key
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 177, Tallow 28, Eighthday, the going of the light down the clay road and the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof. At the going of the light Sella carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke going before her and river wind coming up to meet it, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough and the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie, and gives none of the turns to the basket. She sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without once looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped because nobody under any roof has been given an instruction about the thread, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, stands a moment counting under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, sets the pot rim out with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand, and does not look toward the bed. The widow's mark is untouched because a dusk is not an opening and the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour (T058/T079); the two rooms do not touch. In the small hours he turns out the file the way a man lays instruments on a towel before a case begins, each thing going into its own hollow and nothing resting across anything else. Six hearings of the full note lie beside and never among — five from four sources, a cup across a birth room, a pot in the wheel-shed, the district's slate twice at the Cross and a man giving at the Drawing, and the sixth, the small flat knock out of a person as the men lifted, filed where a thing from a person must go and never among the sources — with no seventh and none invented to fill the empty place (T061/T082). Three near-full answers stand on their own tray, advanced and not paid: a pot under the wheel-shed wall, a rack pot lifted a hand's breadth too high and set down again, and the knowing the wheel-keeper keeps from a kiln-master of the full note a Vail pot would give before it left the wheel, among the near-full and never among the hearings. The older intervals lie at Stone 13, Stone 17 and Stone 25, with the half-beat behind a standing finger, the unchecking stroke that went on over the bright patch and his own held breath from a market morning. On the widened tray nine stoppings — Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23, 26 and 29 — stand as objects and not a rule, intervals and not payments, no payer named to any, with no tenth stood up before the seventh year is earned (T036/T076). The damper lies beside them as one iron with two bites joined to no kiln; the Day 161 fraction, the Day 166 beat under the board and the Day 171 flagstone half-check stand on three separate places, three held changes and not a pair or a doctrine, no word spoken over any and no payer named (T062, T100, T036/T076). The two shut-room tellings stand with no third and the told bell beside the heard bell, four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself (T065/T095, T078 carried). The sixth green is a colour joined to no ear and the foundling a shape with no sale, held offstage and unspent (T050/T051, T033/T034 held). No third gap comes, no fourth likeness is made a cause and no finger of his draws a line between any two absences (T060/T086, T097). Cold arrives in its known order, cheek, temple, the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back, and stops as if it had reached the end of its instruction; the afterdrop waits on the far side of a warming nobody will perform. He wants the crust two inches from his ear, the breast, the pot handle beyond his hand and a number spoken by someone who would have known what a number counted, and gets none of them; he has stopped expecting to be told, which is not the same as not wanting it. The surgeon's register reads the whole of it as an inventory that is not a key and a list that is not a hand: exact, complete and worth nothing at two paces, and he is the only adult in the room and the least use in it (T004, no present-tense break and no tagged memory). One hundred and seventy-seven stands exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool, spoken by nobody (T071/T072); the payer under the floor has had no name for a hundred and seventy-seven days (T088), and the charcoal waits under the shelf for a hand that is not his and a day that has not come (T100).

scenes.title: The Last Working Day
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, sixth dated heading: Day 178, Tallow 29, Ninthday, morning through the going of the light at the kiln mouth, the drying racks, the loaf shelf, the wheel-shed edge and under the Vail roof — the last working day of Tallow before the Account-day. No character anticipates the date and no date is spoken over the basket. The kilns are brought to their last heat of the month; the danger has an order and no name and cannot be carried into a chart — a pot set down wrong gives its high thin note before its time, the dust is ground small as meal under the nails and in the white of a knuckle when a fist opens, and the sweetish edge of lead glaze rides the wrong wind off High Kiln. A potter tells a pot it will do and it is not lost; no lesson is made and no room is changed (T077, T061/T082). At the racks the yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the empty place in the returning line, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Sella moves her lips along the loaf row standing with two unnamed gaps, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and gives nobody a figure; the shelf's two gaps, the fold's one crust and its empty place, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place stay on separate trays, no third gap comes, no fourth likeness is made a cause and no finger of his draws the line (T060/T086, T097). Her finger does not go beneath the board and the charcoal stays unread, awaiting a hand that is not hers to read and a day that has not come (T100). Men unnamed may go low into the finger's-width-open back room before first grey and be given no name; Jorra comes through with slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger, speaks to the wheel, tells a pot You'll do, knows its note and withholds it from a High Kiln kiln-master, and puts the bent finger into the cold iron ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence, holding it until the sentence reaches the pot; nobody speaks of the waiting and the fraction stays a change held and unspoken, not repeated and not made a pair (T035/T031, T062). Tarn takes the broom only after its instruction, sweeps over the shallow bright patch on the flagstones without the half-check and over the collector's road without turning along it; no collector comes, six are counted where the house can check and the seventh held where it cannot, and the loan stays uncalled (T036/T076). The carried fire misses its fifth under the floor with its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy-eight days (T088), the kiln breathes in fours with its gap behind the wall and the river keeps its fifth low note through the finger's-width door — three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). At the going of the light Sella sets him on his bed, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needs, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, sets the pot rim out two inches beyond the reaching hand and leaves the widow's mark untouched, because a shelf and a dusk are not openings (T058/T079). The boy is one hundred and seventy-eight days old and nobody says so, and the count stands exact, complete and unspent (T071/T072).

scenes.title: One in Twelve, as the Notice Says
scenes.synopsis: Seventh entry, seventh dated heading: Day 179, Tallow 30, Tenthday, the third Account-day of Tallow and the last market of the firing month, dawn through afternoon at the Cross — the reading block under the moot-post, the pot board across the square, the out-of-line landing below the north bridge. **The chapter's one meaningful change:** the month's last Account-day is lived and read over the boy, and Sella sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lies and stands a half-pace off, a displacement made without a word and without a reason given to the basket. Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one corner of his mouth, wipes his thumb twice on his apron before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure and reads one in twelve, as the notice says low into the crowd; he says The levy is called. It is not called by me and your house, never I, and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness. The printed figure stands unchallenged; a figure read aloud is still not the figure paid, and the figure that goes into the slate does not know the hand that went in on Seed 15 and did not come out (T015/T041/T047, T077, T098 carried). The bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept beside the told bell (T078). Hessa Rale of Slate Row comes through with Berr's narrow slate held edge-on to her forearm and the writing turned to her sleeve, her hand to the slate before her eyes go to the crowd; to a woman who asks what she carries she says I don't read it. I carry it. There's a difference, and the road doesn't care which and Cross to Greybank. Reading goes up before noon. I've got a road to walk, without rudeness or apology. No figure comes off the slate; she is a runner and not a reader, her record-first order of reaching an eighth such hand filed on a place of its own, advanced and not paid, joined to no other keeping (T080). Below the north bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing with his cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, his slate to his forearm with the writing inward and his hand to the slate before his eyes go to the stalls, entering a figure before he looks at the man who gave it, for a measure nobody called (T090). Across the square at the pot board a silent woman turns a cup a quarter and sets it back exactly where it stood with the sweetish green of lead glaze at one corner of her mouth, unnamed, given no dialogue and never Fenna in narration; the green stays a colour joined to no ear (T050/T051 held, not paid). At the market's edge the foundling is not seen — a shape with no sale and his sixth glimpse unspent, no loaf passing, no slate opened within reach of the basket and no secret sold (T033/T034 held). Sella keeps the half-pace from every open slate and gives the instruction to the wool, the river wind and the running water, never to the basket; nothing under the Reading is joined, named, opened, called or paid (T058/T079). The carried fire's payer has had no name for a hundred and seventy-nine days (T088), and the boy is one hundred and seventy-nine days old and five months and twenty-nine days, told by nobody (T071/T072).

scenes.title: Four, Four and a Gap into Ember
scenes.synopsis: Eighth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 179, Tallow 30, Tenthday, the going of the light down the clay road and the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof. At the going of the light Sella carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke going before her and the river wind coming up to meet it, the two passing on the stair of the evening as they have passed every evening of his life without a word spent on either, the carrying arm keeping the weight in muscle and giving no account of the cost. She goes wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough where the water is called weather, the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie, and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number and no explanation of the turns to the basket (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, base first and the weight settled the way a woman sets a vessel that must not rock, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without once looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped because nobody under any roof has been given an instruction about the thread, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed before it goes away, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, stands a moment with the back of the pot in her hand counting under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot rim out with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed. The widow's mark hangs where it hung and is not touched, because a dusk is not an opening and the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour (T058/T079); the two rooms do not touch. In the small hours he turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel: six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh and none invented, five from four sources and the sixth from a person; three near-full answers advanced and not paid; the older intervals; nine stoppings as objects and not a rule with no tenth before the seventh year is earned (T061/T082, T036/T076). The damper lies beside them as one iron with two bites joined to no kiln, with no word in Grathic that would carry both mercies in one mouthful (T062). The Day 161 fraction at the damper, the Day 166 held beat beneath the loaf shelf and the Day 171 flagstone half-check stand on three separate places, three held changes and not a pair or a doctrine, no payer named to any (T062, T100, T036/T076); the two shut-room tellings stand with no third (T065/T095), and the told bell beside the heard bell, four, four and a gap, with nobody crossing himself (T078). In the other room the one stiff brown-edged crust lies leathery two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; the loaf shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps and the charcoal waits under the front edge for a hand that is not his and a day that has not come (T060/T086, T100); the shallow pan's gone place keeps its round ring on a tray of its own and the field's empty place stays where the yard went around it, neither laid across the shelf's gaps, the fold's crust or the sixth green, which is a colour joined to no ear, while the foundling is a shape with no sale offstage (T097, T098, T050/T051, T033/T034 held). No third gap comes, no fourth likeness is made a cause and no finger of his draws a line between any two of them. Through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings and never invented to stand up as a seventh; through the floor the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer without a name for a hundred and seventy-nine days; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb. Three counts in three places, and none rises up and becomes the others. Ash lies thin along the skirting board in the colour of the clean dark line and the new finer grey called the thaw lies beside it, neither swept at this hour and neither with an instruction. Cold arrives cheek, temple, the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back, and stops; the afterdrop waits. He wants the crust, the breast, the pot handle two inches beyond his hand and a number spoken by somebody who would have known what a number counted, and gets none of them; he has stopped expecting to be told, which is not the same as not wanting it. The figure read is not the figure paid, the box has gone up the clay road locked, the cord and knot-string and second twist stay unread, the clerk stays set for his uncalled measure, the sixth green stays a colour and the foundling a shape. One hundred and seventy-nine stands exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool, spoken by nobody under any roof (T071/T072). The surgeon's register reads the whole of it as an inventory that is not a key and a list that is not a hand; the reading is exact and worth nothing at two paces. His hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water over water through the finger's-width door and comes down against the fold. Nothing is joined, paid, named, opened, called, spent or ended; the firing month goes out without a boundary drawn and the count goes forward into Ember with the fire's fifth still missing and the charcoal still waiting under the shelf for a hand that is not his and a day that has not come (T004, no present-tense break and no tagged remembered line).
